_about:
Event write-ups written for GeoHistory (AI-written from the sources listed with each entry; shown in the
app with that label). One JSON file per batch in t1/. Each entry, keyed by the event id of data/events:

  "title", "y" (must equal the event's year), "place" (as in the event record),
  "paras": 2-5 short paragraphs (who and on which side; what happened, step by step; why; what it led to),
  "sources": [{"url", "title", "publisher", "accessed", "supports": [claim numbers]}]  every URL was fetched,
  "claims": ["claim 1", ...]  the factual claims in the text, numbered from 1, each supported by a source,
  "disagree": where sources differ (also said in the text), or null,
  "checked": null, or {"by": source url not used for writing, "result": "...", "errors": n} after the
             random re-check.

Britannica (403), the Oxford DNB (403), the Imperial War Museums (403), the British Museum (403) and
Smithsonian Magazine (403) refuse automated fetches from this build's network, so they are not cited.
Text is never copied from copyrighted pages; Wikipedia text is summarised with attribution.
_process: Checks before an entry is added: (1) every claim is matched to a source that was fetched (tools/context/writeup_add.py checks the numbering); (2) every claim backed by one source only is searched for in the other source's text, and every date or number found in only one source must be confirmed in Wikipedia or a third fetched source, or stated as that source's figure, or removed; a flagged date is never kept on memory alone (rule added after two errors in re-checks, both single-source HISTORY.com dates); (3) a re-check of at least 2% of each batch's claims against a source not used for writing, recorded in 'checked'; if a batch's re-check error rate is above 2%, writing stops until the process is fixed.
